prompt:
A hero portrait for a card game's character-select screen, made by hand like a 1993 fantasy trading-card or game-book illustration, the same look as the game's cards: confident black pen-and-ink outlines around every shape, ink hatching in the shadows, filled with flat, slightly blotchy gouache and watercolour washes, visible brush marks and the rough off-white paper grain showing through, colours a little faded and misregistered like an old printed card. A limited palette of 4 or 5 colours, dark overall. Stylised and graphic with bold simple shapes, not realistic: no smooth skin rendering, no soft glow, no rim light, no sunset glare, no depth of field, no oil-painting polish, no 3D, not modern digital concept art, not a heroic movie poster. Not head-on and not looking at the viewer: the figure is seen from an angle, caught in a moment of their story. Head and upper body fill the square and may be cropped by the edges; the background is simple and dark and falls to near-black at the edges so it sits on a dark screen. No text, no letters, no border, no frame, no logo.

Subject: Odysseus, king of Ithaca, seen in three-quarter view from slightly below and to the side, standing at the stern of his black Greek ship and gripping the steering oar, his head turned away over his shoulder as he looks back across the wine-dark sea, eyes narrowed and calculating. A weathered, bearded man in a simple felt sailor's cap and a patched, salt-stained cloak over plain bronze armour. Night sea, a single pale moon, the ship's painted eye on the hull at the edge of the picture. Greek in every detail, colours of deep sea blue, black and dull bronze.
